thread:
Noah Rivera: Need quick guidance - traveling to Tokyo for customer kickoff tomorrow but passport visa sticker delayed by customs. I received an emergency e-visa approval email and printed boarding pass but the airline needs visa proof at check-in. I paid a same-day visa expedite fee and courier charge to get documents overnight. Can I expense the expedite + courier?
Maria (People Ops): Yes, expedite fees and courier costs for required travel docs are reimbursable if travel is business-approved. Attach the e-visa approval email, courier receipt, and proof of payment.
Noah Rivera: The airline also charged a same-day ticket change fee because I had to adjust arrival time. Is that covered?
Sam Patel (Finance): Covered if change was necessary for the business trip. Provide the original ticket, new ticket receipt, proof of payment, and manager note approving the change (can be retro). We'll only reimburse net incremental cost.
Noah Rivera: Got it. Also: how to code this in Expensely quickly?
Sam Patel (Finance): Copy these fields:
```
Expense type: "Visa & Travel Document Fees"
Project/Cost center: "Sales - APAC"
GL account: "5105 - Travel Admin"
Description: "Emergency visa expedite and courier for Tokyo customer kickoff; ticket change fee included"
Required attachments: evisa_email.pdf, courier_receipt.pdf, ticket_new.pdf, ticket_old.pdf, proof_of_payment.pdf, manager_approval.pdf
```
travel-bot: Reminder: redact passport number on uploaded images. Maximum 10MB per file. If refund occurs later, finance will reconcile.
Noah Rivera: Thanks — filing now, will include manager note.
Maria (People Ops): Safe travels!
